MUQATIL:78:17-20/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:78:17-20/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:78:17-20/r1.claim: The appointed Day of Decision is the Judgment between creatures and the fixed time for unbelievers' promised recompense, answering their question in 36:48.

TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r1.claim: The Day of Decision is the appointed day when God separates the earliest and latest generations by their deeds; the verse “day the Horn is blown” explains that appointed event.

TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says the ṣūr is a horn.

TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p18#2/r3.claim: Qatāda interprets the ṣūr as creation or created beings.

NAHHAS:v5p127/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p127/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p127/r3.claim: Mīqāt is kāna's predicate; outside the Qur'an kāna could be inoperative and the word raised.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r1.claim: The Day of Decision is the Resurrection, named because judgment separates earlier and later people and those rewarded from those punished.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r2.claim: Miqat can mean an appointed time for people to gather.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r3.claim: Miqat can mean the time set for reward and punishment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r1.claim: The Day of Decision is the appointed time for judgment among creation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r2.claim: The appointed time is for the prophets and messengers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r3.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p125/r3.claim: Another explanation is that it is the appointed time for the promised reward and punishment.

JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r4.claim: Al-faṣl is the decisive judgment and originally means cutting; the Day is named for God's judgment between creatures, like the Day of Conquest.

JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r5.claim: Mīqāt is a set time for an event; the pattern names the thing by which an event is timed, like mīʿād from a promise and mīzān from weighing.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p313#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p313#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p313#2/r3.claim: The Day of Decision is judgment among creation and the appointed time for promised reward and punishment.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p687#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p687#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p687#2/r1.claim: The appointed time is a boundary fixed in God's decree at which the world ends, or a boundary toward which all creatures are gathered.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r1.claim: يوم الفصل is the Resurrection, when God separates believers from unbelievers and truth from falsehood.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r2.claim: ميقات is a time-word on the pattern مفعال, like ميعاد from وعد.

TABRISI:78:17-30/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:78:17-30/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:78:17-30/r12.claim: Miqat is the endpoint of a fixed time appointed for an event, formed like mi'ad from promise and miqdar from measure.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#2/r1.claim: The Day of Decision is the Day God judges among creatures and the appointed time for the promised reward and punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:78:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:17-18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:17-18/r1.claim: The Day of Decision is the appointed time and gathering for earlier and later peoples to receive promised recompense; God separates His creatures then.

BAYDAWI-FULL:78:17-18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:17-18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:17-18/r1.claim: The Day of Decision is fixed in God’s knowledge or judgment, marking the end of worldly life or the point all creatures reach.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#16/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#16/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#16/r1.claim: The Day of Decision separates benefactor from wrongdoer and truth from falsehood; it is a fixed endpoint for recompense or an appointed time for reward and punishment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r10.claim: The day of decision is Judgment, separating truth and falsehood; it is God's appointed limit at the world's end and the creatures' destination.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p299/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p299/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p299/r1.claim: The signs of power and wisdom establish divine oneness, stirring obedient believers to long for God and wrongdoers to fear meeting Him.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p299/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p299/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p299/r2.claim: The Day of Decision is the great announcement and a fixed terminus in God’s knowledge, when creation is gathered and every ambiguity is settled by delivering the wronged from the oppressor.

DURR-FULL:v8p392/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r14.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r14.claim: Qatada says the Day of Decision is an appointed time, when God magnifies the day and judges the earlier and later peoples.

BURSEVI:v10p231/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p231/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p231/r2.claim: The Day of Decision is God’s division of creatures into the blessed and wretched according to differences and correspondences in their dispositions, forms, character, and deeds.

BURSEVI:v10p231/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p231/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p231/r3.claim: Its appointment belongs to God’s primordial knowledge and decree, before temporal time; the appointed moment of resurrection and recompense cannot be advanced or delayed.

BURSEVI:v10p231/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p231/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p231/r4.claim: Miqat is more specific than time in general: it is the fixed time when resurrection and the promised reward and punishment appear.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r1.claim: The verse begins explaining why the Resurrection is delayed and answers mockers who ask when the promised event will come; another says proof of resurrection naturally invites a timing question, which the author deems weak.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r2.claim: The Day of Decision is a fixed appointment in God's knowledge for raising all generations and assigning reward or punishment, which cannot be advanced or delayed.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r3.claim: Alternatively it is the appointed limit at which worldly life ends, or the limit all creatures reach as their conditions are distinguished; the first explanation better fits the context.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#3/r4.claim: كان may refer to God's prior knowledge, or function as a past form for a certain future event.

ELMALILI:78:14-30/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r4.claim: The appointed Day of Decision concludes the signs just established: waking, harvest, and the end of worldly life, resolving disputes and accounting for blessings.

ELMALILI:78:14-30/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r5.claim: These signs should make people understand the day's coming, otherwise they will later know it with certainty; its time is fixed in divine knowledge.

ELMALILI:78:14-30/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r6.claim: The Day of Decision is certainly coming and is an unfailing appointment, as also stated in al-Mursalat.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r1.claim: The announcement of the Day of Decision explains the opening question about the great news; placing it after crops produced by rain makes their emergence an image for resurrection.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r2.claim: The Day of Decision is the day of resurrection and recompense; the confirmed statement counters the disbelievers' denial.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r3.claim: Fasl means separating what is mixed, then came to mean distinguishing ambiguous matters and adjudicating; recompense separates people from one another.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r4.claim: Calling it the Day of Decision confirms both resurrection and recompense and God's judgment among people over their disputes and mutual wrongs.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r5.claim: The verb ‘was’ makes the appointed time established in God's wisdom, so their demand cannot bring it forward.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p29/r6.claim: Miqat derives from time and means a fixed time; here the context supplies resurrection and recompense as what has its appointed time.

TABATABAI:78:17-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:17-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:78:17-20/r1.claim: This section describes the promised Day of Decision, what happens to the transgressors and the godfearing, and concludes with a warning.

TABATABAI:78:17-20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:17-20/r2.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:78:17-20/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines mīqāt as the endpoint of a fixed measure of time at which an event occurs, formed from waqt as mīʿād is from waʿd.

TABATABAI:78:17-20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:17-20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:78:17-20/r3.claim: The Day of Decision divides judgment among people so each group receives what its deeds merit; kāna and the emphatic inna show that God knew and fixed this endpoint when creating the cosmos.

ASAD-NOTES:78:17#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:78:17#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:78:17#n9/r1.claim: Asad connects this passage with vv.4-5 and note 6 on 78:13.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r1.claim: Paired with al-Mursalat, this surah uses divine providence in the heavens and earth to establish Judgment as the necessary end of a purposeful world, rewarding the God-fearing and punishing rebels.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r2.claim: The surahs share an affirmative-question style aimed at deniers; each verse reproaches them while believers' glad tidings are understood against the warning.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r4.claim: The signs of providence, mercy, wisdom, and power throughout earth and heavens show that humanity is not unchecked or unaccountable; its fixed day of reckoning must arrive.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p139/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p139/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p139/r1.claim: Created signs display God’s power, providence, mercy, wisdom, and oneness; reflection on them leads to certainty that judgment has a fixed time.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p142/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p142/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p142/r6.claim: The appointed Judgment sums up the argument: the provider gathers humanity, judges who recognized or ignored His favors, and rewards or punishes them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p143/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p143/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p143/r1.claim: The placement of judgment after the signs shows that the world’s system proclaims that day; sun, moon, clouds, and winds serve human needs.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r1.claim: The appointed Day of Decision separates truth from falsehood, the just from the unjust, and believers from deniers, then repays worldly deeds with perfect justice.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r2.claim: At the time of resurrection known only to God, people and all creatures gather, and God judges them so worldly injustices receive their due.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:17/r3.claim: The verse can also be understood to say that the appointed meeting day will itself be the day of judgment.

STUDYQURAN:78:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:78:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:78:17/r1.claim: The Day of Division is Resurrection, when truth and falsehood, right and wrong, and light and dark are finally distinguished.

STUDYQURAN:78:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:78:17/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:78:17/r2.claim: The appointed Moment is guaranteed; God will not fail the tryst.
